serves.statement: keep base:2 (Placeholder base T, Allied) at 10 days of supply, a run every 15 days

reason.worked: Reading today at base:2: 10 t over 1 t a day = 10 days, against a floor of 10 days. A run ordered on day 1 loads on day 1 (0.32 hours at the source = 1 day), sails on day 2, and is due at base:2 on day 2. Without it the reading of day 3 is 8 t against 10 days x 1 t = 10 t: below the floor, so a run is needed. The stock projected for the reading of day 2 is 9 t. Load = max(0, 10 - 9) + 15 (15 days of use) = 16 t. Ships ship:1: 1 x the pool's free ships in number order = a room that covers the load. Passage 200 nm out at 16 kn = 12.5 hours, 1 day; 200 nm back = 12.5 hours, 1 day; unloading 16 t at base:2 = 0.8 hours, 1 day. Back at the source at hour 60.5 of the run and fuelled by hour 60.75 (0.25 hours at 200 t an hour), its ships are free on day 5, the morning after the day the fuelling ends. The staff adds this run to the plan.
would_change: a reading of day 3 at or above 10 t would call no run
a free ship of the pool earlier in number order would carry it instead
